reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder of purine synthesis caused by variants in ADSL, encoding adenylosuccinate lyase
The enzyme acts at two steps of purine metabolism, so its deficiency causes accumulation of the dephosphorylated succinylpurines SAICA-riboside and succinyladenosine in body fluids
The biochemical hallmark is elevated succinylpurines in urine and cerebrospinal fluid, detectable with a modified Bratton-Marshall test or by chromatography
Clinical phenotypes range from a severe neonatal form with seizures and encephalopathy to childhood forms with psychomotor delay, epilepsy and autistic behaviour
Prominent autistic features and self-injurious or stereotyped behaviour are characteristic of the milder phenotypes
The ratio of succinyladenosine to SAICA-riboside broadly correlates with clinical severity
Muscle wasting, growth impairment and epilepsy are common accompanying features
There is no established curative treatment, and management is supportive
reference.pathophysiology: Adenylosuccinate lyase catalyses two reactions in purine metabolism: the conversion of SAICAR to AICAR in de novo purine synthesis, and the conversion of adenylosuccinate to AMP in the purine nucleotide cycle. Enzyme deficiency blocks these steps, leading to accumulation of the phosphorylated precursors, which are dephosphorylated to the succinylpurines SAICA-riboside and succinyladenosine. These accumulated metabolites are thought to be neurotoxic and to impair normal purine nucleotide availability, disrupting cerebral development and function. The degree of residual enzyme activity and the relative accumulation of each metabolite influence the severity of the neurological phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Early-onset epileptic encephalopathies of other causes
Other inborn errors of purine or pyrimidine metabolism
Mitochondrial disorders with developmental delay and seizures
additionalInvestigations: Urine and cerebrospinal fluid screening for succinylpurines (modified Bratton-Marshall test)
Quantitation of SAICA-riboside and succinyladenosine with calculation of their ratio
Enzyme activity assay in fibroblasts or liver
Electroencephalography and brain MRI to characterise seizures and structural change
redFlags: Neonatal seizures with encephalopathy and profound hypotonia
Marked autistic and self-injurious behaviour with global delay
Failure to thrive with muscle wasting
reference.prognosis: The neonatal-onset form is severe and often fatal in early life. Childhood-onset forms cause variable but usually significant intellectual disability, epilepsy and behavioural problems that persist, as no disease-modifying therapy is currently available.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis by not screening urine for succinylpurines in unexplained autism with epilepsy
Attributing the presentation solely to idiopathic autism or cerebral palsy
Overlooking milder phenotypes with predominantly behavioural features
Assuming a normal metabolic screen excludes the disorder without specific purine testing
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Provide supportive multidisciplinary care, as no disease-modifying therapy is currently available
Control seizures with appropriate anticonvulsant therapy
Support development and behaviour with early intervention, educational support and behavioural strategies for autistic and self-injurious features
Support nutrition and safe feeding where feeding difficulties arise
Recognise that trialled supplements such as D-ribose, uridine or S-adenosylmethionine have not shown proven benefit
Monitor with electroencephalography, brain imaging and developmental assessment
Offer genetic counselling with carrier testing and prenatal or preimplantation options for this autosomal recessive disorder
